sections.h2: How big is Suffolk, Virginia, and where is it?
sections.html:
Suffolk is the largest city in Virginia by land area, with about 399 square miles of land and another 30 square miles of water. It sits in the Hampton Roads region, on the Nansemond and James rivers, and holds part of the Great Dismal Swamp.

Suffolk combines a downtown, a northern corridor tied to defense work and long rural stretches, and 27.1% of residents lived in areas the census counted as rural in 2020.

A house in Suffolk can therefore mean a downtown bungalow, a house near the Harborview area in the north or a farmhouse on a country road. Each one sells differently.

sections.h2: How did Suffolk become one large city?
sections.html:
Suffolk was founded in 1742 as a port on the Nansemond River, first called Constant's Warehouse. It incorporated as a city in 1910 and, in 1974, merged with the independent city of Nansemond, which had been Nansemond County until 1972.

The merger brought in the towns of Holland and Whaleyville. The city is now divided into seven boroughs: Chuckatuck, Cypress, Holy Neck, Nansemond, Sleepy Hole, Suffolk and Whaleyville.

The boroughs are political districts, not neighborhoods, but sellers often use the borough or the old community name to describe where a house is.

sections.h2: What does Suffolk's housing and population look like?
sections.html:
Suffolk's population rose from 84,585 in 2010 to 94,324 in 2020, and the Census Bureau estimated 104,699 in 2025. The city counted 38,364 housing units in 2020.

Around half of Suffolk households (50.7%) were married-couple households in 2020, and 33.5% had children under 18.

sections.h2: What jobs and employers shape Suffolk's housing market?
sections.html:
Suffolk's economy rests on distribution, manufacturing, farming, health care and defense work. Peanut processing has been a local industry for over a century, and Planters Peanuts began in the city in 1912.

  • Sentara Obici Hospital, completed in 2002 as Louise Obici Memorial Hospital, is a major health employer.
  • Other large employers listed on Wikipedia include Unilever, Lipton, Massimo Zanetti Beverage Group, Walmart, Target and QVC.
  • Defense contractors and Navy commands cluster in the north end near US 17 and Interstate 664. The Joint Forces Command base there was disestablished in 2011, and some of its functions continued in the same buildings.

The same page estimated about 1,000 added jobs, counting military, civilians and contractors, from Navy cyber commands moving into the vacated buildings.

sections.h2: How do Suffolk's roads and rivers affect a house?
sections.html:
Suffolk is served by US 13, 17, 58, 258 and 460, State Route 10 and Interstate 664, which crosses the northeastern edge of the city. The Monitor-Merrimac Memorial Bridge-Tunnel links the city to Newport News and was completed in 1992.

The city took over its own road system from the Virginia Department of Transportation on July 1, 2006, as is customary for independent cities. That means roads and drainage ditches in Suffolk are a city responsibility.

Water matters here. A house near the Nansemond, the swamp or low farmland may sit in a flood zone, and buyers or their insurers will ask. Check FEMA's flood map for your parcel before you talk to any buyer.

sections.h2: What is Suffolk's climate, and what does it do to older houses?
sections.html:
Suffolk has hot, humid summers and mild to cool winters. NOAA normals for 1991 to 2020 show about 51.8 inches of rain a year, with July highs near 87 degrees and a record high of 105.

  • More than 120 days a year bring measurable rain, which tests gutters, grading and crawl spaces.
  • Snow is light, at about 5.8 inches a year, so winter roof loads are rarely the worry.
  • Humidity is the steady problem, showing up as mold, wood rot and failing HVAC systems.

Those are the repairs a cash buyer prices in, and the ones a conventional buyer's inspector will list.

sections.h2: What schools, transit and sights come with a Suffolk address?
sections.html:
Suffolk Public Schools runs 12 elementary schools, four middle schools, three high schools and one alternative school. Nansemond-Suffolk Academy is a private college preparatory school, and Paul D. Camp Community College has a campus in the city.

The city operates Suffolk Transit, a local bus service with two connections to Hampton Roads Transit buses. Amtrak's Northeast Regional between Norfolk and Petersburg passes the old Norfolk and Western station without stopping, so most commuters drive.

  • The Seaboard Station Railroad Museum at 326 North Main Street sits in a former railroad station.
  • Suffolk hosts the Peanut Fest each fall, a tradition since 1977.
  • Riddick's Folly, the Suffolk Historic District and the Driver Historic District are on the list of local attractions.

Mention the schools and the commute when you talk to a buyer, since both are usual questions for a Suffolk house.

sections.h2: What does a Suffolk seller pay at closing?
sections.html:
Virginia's deed taxes apply in Suffolk like anywhere else in the state. The state recordation tax is 25 cents per $100 under section 58.1-801, and the grantor's tax is 50 cents per $500 under section 58.1-802.

The grantor's tax falls on the seller, and the clerk who records the deed splits it between the state and the locality. If an owner is behind on city taxes, ask the Suffolk Treasurer for a payoff figure, since we could not confirm a Suffolk tax calendar from an opened city page.

  • Request a title search early so liens surface before the closing date.
  • Confirm tax proration on the settlement statement.
  • Keep copies of the deed, the closing statement and the payoff letters.

sections.h2: Do special rules apply to an inherited or estate house in Suffolk?
sections.html:
They can. The Residential Property Disclosure Act excludes transfers by a fiduciary during the administration of an estate, guardianship, conservatorship or trust, under section 55.1-702.

Foreclosure sales and sales between spouses or to family in the direct line are also excluded. An estate attorney can tell you whether your sale falls inside the list.

sections.h2: When is a cash sale the right choice in Suffolk?
sections.html:
A cash sale suits houses that would struggle in a financed sale, such as one with storm damage, deferred maintenance, tenants or title questions. It also helps owners who live out of the area, since there is little to coordinate.

It is not the only good route. A listing can bring more money for a house in strong condition, if you can wait and pay for repairs. Compare the final net, not the headline offer.

faqs.q: Is Suffolk the biggest city in Virginia?
faqs.a: By land area, yes. Suffolk has about 399 square miles of land, the most of any city in Virginia. Virginia Beach has a larger total area because of its water, and a much larger population.
Suffolk has seven boroughs: Chuckatuck, Cypress, Holy Neck, Nansemond, Sleepy Hole, Suffolk and Whaleyville. They are political districts used for city council and school board seats.

faqs.q: Do I need to repair my Suffolk house before selling for cash?
faqs.a: No. Cash buyers generally buy as is, so you can skip repairs and cleaning. A listing usually needs repairs to satisfy buyers' inspections and lenders.

faqs.q: Who pays Virginia's grantor's tax on a Suffolk sale?
faqs.a: The seller does unless the parties agree otherwise. The tax is 50 cents per $500 of value under Virginia Code 58.1-802.

faqs.q: How many people live in Suffolk, Virginia?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 94,324 residents, and the Census Bureau estimated 104,699 for July 1, 2025. That makes Suffolk the tenth most populous city in Virginia as of 2020.

faqs.q: Where can I confirm Suffolk's real estate tax dates?
faqs.a: Ask the Suffolk Treasurer or Commissioner of the Revenue. We left the dates out because we could not confirm them from an opened city page.
